picked.t: 베트남·칠레, ‘전략적 동반자 관계’ 격상…정치·경제·농업·과학기술 등 6대 협력 축 설정
picked.body: 또 럼 베트남 공산당 서기장(오른쪽)과 호세 안토니오 카스트 칠레 대통령이 정상회담 뒤 공동 기자회견 중인 모습. (사진=TTXVN) 베트남과 칠레가 양국 관계를 전략적 동반자 관계로 격상하기로 합의했다. 또 럼(To Lam) 베트남 공산당 서기장 겸 국가주석은 16일 호세 안토니오 카스트 칠레 대통령과의 정상회담 뒤 공동 기자회견에서 이 같은 양국 관계 격상을 발표했다. 양국은 새로운 협력 관계 내 △정치·외교 △경제·무역 △농업 △과학기술 △교육·문화 △국방·안보를 6대 협력 축으로 삼기로 했다. 공동 기자회견에서 럼 서기장은 “그동안의 양국 협력 성과와 아시아·태평양에 대한 양국의 공동 전략 비전을 바탕으로 관계를 격상하기로 했다”고 설명했다. 양국은 새 관계의 방향과 목표, 원칙, 협력 축을 정했으며, 각자의 지경학적 이점을 살려 동아시아와 중남미 사이의 운송·물류, 자금 흐름, 공급망 연결을 강화하기로 했다. 이를 통해 양국 기업에 더 많은 기회를 만든다는 구상이다. 협력 분야는 무역, 투자, 농업, 전략 광물, 과학기술, 운송·물류·공급망 연결, 금융·은행, 관광, 국방·안보 등으로 넓혔다. 양국은 세무·관세, 과학기술, 국방·안보 등의 협력 협상을 이어가 협력을 넓힐 틀을 마련하고 지역·국제 현안도 논의하기로 했다. 양국 정상은 항행·항공의 자유와 안전을 유지하고 분쟁을 평화적으로 해결하는 데 뜻을 같이하며, 유엔헌장과 1982년 유엔해양법협약을 비롯한 국제법을 존중해야 한다는 입장도 확인했다. 럼 서기장은 이번 관계 격상이 양국이 각자의 잠재력과 강점을 더 잘 살리는 동력과 기반이 될 것이라고 확신을 표명했다. 카스트 대통령은 “협력 관계 격상이 양측의 전략적 비전을 보여준다”며 “양국은 앞으로도 양자 협력 협정 이행을 지속적으로 추진해 나갈 것”이라고 강조했다. 그는 이어 광업 협력을 강화하고 투자를 넓히며 양국 항만 체계를 연결하길 바란다고 말했다. 양국 기업이 산업·기술 분야 협력을 늘리고 시장을 넓혀 양국 경제가 기대에 걸맞게 성장하길 기대한다고도 했다. 앞서 카스트 칠레 대통령 부부는 럼 서기장의 초청에 따라 15~17일 사흘간 일정으로 베트남을 공식 방문한 바 있다. 이번 방문은 카스트 대통령 취임 후 첫 베트남 방문이다. 칠레는 남미에서 가장 먼저 베트남과 수교한 나라 가운데 하나로, 양국은 지난 2007년 5월 포괄적 동반자 관계를 맺었다.

picked.t: What’s next for Vietnam after hitting $1 trillion trade milestone?
picked.body: It exceeded $1.01 trillion as of October, a 32.3% increase year-on-year. The National Statistics Office said the milestone reflected the economy’s openness and deep integration into global markets. The speed of growth is a highlight. It took Vietnam more than a decade to raise trade from $100 billion in 2007 to $500 billion in 2019. But it took only seven more years to double that figure. The statistics office attributed the acceleration to expanded production capacity, investment inflows, manufacturing growth in, and more effective use of free trade agreements (FTAs). Vietnam has joined 19 FTAs, which contributed to the rise in foreign investment. In the year to date, FDI has been a 17-year high of nearly $55 billion, with manufacturing accounting for 51.6%. Electronics, computers, machinery, equipment, spare parts, and phones and phone components accounted for more than half of all exports. Their share could rise further amid a boom in AI investment. There are several indicators that point to further trade growth. In a recent survey of 22 electronics manufacturers, recruitment firm Navigos Search found that 82% planned to expand their workforces over the next 12 months. Their hiring needs ranged from production workers and quality control engineers to research and development specialists. To meet the growing demand for transporting high-value goods such as semiconductors, servers, and AI components, express delivery company Federal Express this month added 567 metric tons of weekly air cargo capacity between the Asia-Pacific and the U.S. The expansion gives shipments from Vietnam an additional route through Clark International Airport in the Philippines besides the Hanoi–Bangkok service. Ee-Hui Tan, Federal Express managing director of operations for Vietnam and Cambodia, said businesses need reliable cargo capacity as they expand in major markets. Surveys also point to a positive trade outlook. S&P Global’s Purchasing Managers’ Index report in October showed that manufacturers in Vietnam were optimistic about output over the next 12 months. Business confidence reached an eight-month high though admittedly below levels seen before the Middle East conflict. HSBC’s newly released Global Trade Survey 2026, which polled 10,000 senior executives in 26 markets, found that businesses in Vietnam and the Philippines were the most optimistic about international trade, with 94% expecting their operations to grow over the next two years compared with 86% globally. In Vietnam, 97% of businesses said measures they had recently taken to address trade uncertainty and disruptions had been effective. Nearly all were using at least one FTA. But challenges remain. Tariffs were the most frequently cited cost factor by Vietnamese businesses, at 52% as against 43% globally. Energy costs ranked second, at 49%, also above the global figure. Some 97% said barriers prevented them from making greater use of FTAs. Andrew Harker, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said new orders rose in October, but at a slower pace than in September. "While firms are able to maintain improvements for now, they will be hoping for a more conducive environment for growth in the months ahead." Shifting market trends, tougher buyer requirements, and hiring difficulties are also putting pressure on businesses. More than half of the 22 electronics manufacturers surveyed by Navigos Search said they faced high competition in hiring workers. Manufacturing workers are expected to be the hardest to recruit over the next three to five years, 73% of respondents said. They were followed by R&D engineers and specialists (50%) and automation engineers (36%). The bigger question is how much of that trillion-dollar trade Vietnam can retain. The figure measures the total value of goods crossing the border. But since production still relies heavily on imported materials and components, the figure does not capture the value created within Vietnam. At an event held as part of the Autumn Economic Forum (AEF 2026) last month, Mariam J. Sherman, the World Bank’s country director for Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos, said foreign businesses accounted for 73% of exports. Vietnamese businesses and workers retained little of the value generated by the country’s exports, she added. The statistics office said, as trade grows, Vietnam needs to strengthen domestic production capacity, increase indigenous content, and raise the share of value added by Vietnamese businesses. The next phase should be judged by the quality of trade growth in the form of greater contributions by domestic businesses, products with more advanced technology and higher value added, more self-reliant supply chains, more diverse markets, and growth that better protects the environment. Also at the forum, Fazurin Jamaludin, the International Monetary Fund’s resident representative for Vietnam and Laos, said Vietnam’s total factor productivity has been trending downward recently.
